drhp.business: The Company is engaged in the manufacturing and trading of ceramic, vitrified and allied tile products, with manufacturing facilities at Sira and Karaikal. Its range spans ceramic wall and floor tiles and vitrified tiles including GVT and PGVT in larger formats, sold to residential, commercial and institutional construction demand. Sales are made through an established distribution network supported by dealers, architects, builders and other channel partners.

risks.note: MD&A Risks & Concerns names fluctuations in raw material and energy costs as a principal exposure; Opportunities & Threats attributes rising energy and raw material costs to Middle East geopolitical tension, the Russia-Ukraine situation and US-initiated trade tariffs, which 'continue to pose challenges to cost management'. Tile manufacture is energy-intensive and the Directors' Report cites energy costs and logistics expenses among the year's challenges.
risks.risk: Raw material and energy cost inflation

risks.note: The Company operates in a competitive and dynamic environment against both organized and unorganized tile makers; MD&A states 'competitive intensity, coupled with pricing pressures, may impact margins'.
risks.risk: Competitive intensity and pricing pressure on margins

risks.note: MD&A flags that economic conditions, developments in the real estate and construction sectors, and changes in consumer preferences may impact performance; end-demand is housing, commercial real estate and infrastructure led, so a macroeconomic slowdown transmits directly to volumes.
risks.risk: Demand cyclicality tied to real estate and construction

risks.note: Risks & Concerns lists supply chain disruptions; the production-plan review during the year explicitly identified temporary raw material supply constraints and availability of energy as reasons the approved plan had to be revised.
risks.risk: Supply chain disruption and raw material / energy availability

risks.note: Credit risks are named in MD&A Risks & Concerns, and the trade receivables turnover ratio deteriorated to 4.46 from 7.12 (a 37.28% variance) with the stated remark 'There is increase in receivable during the year'.

The business is stated to be subject to regulatory, environmental and statutory compliance requirements, and MD&A adds that changes in government policies and environmental regulations could affect demand and business performance.
risks.risk: Regulatory, environmental and statutory compliance exposure

risks.note: MD&A cites the outbreak of war in the Middle East, the Iran-America and Ukraine-Russia conflicts, US-initiated trade tariffs and uncertainties in global trade as factors that already forced a comprehensive review of the approved production plan and altered customer order forecasts and export opportunities.
risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict and global trade / tariff uncertainty

risks.note: The debt equity ratio rose to 0.20 from 0.11, an 84.40% variance, with the stated reason 'There is increase in new borrowings for new project' — the expansion is debt-funded, and the Board withheld a dividend for FY26 to retain profits for working capital and future expansion.
